text:
alex: heads up — product wants a new set of runtime dashboards for the rollout UX metrics. they want per-route latency, token cost, and fallback counts surfaced by next sprint. who owns the exporter + aggregation plan?
maya: i can take exporter changes (runtime side). needs to expose per-request metadata: model_id, route, batch_size, kv_cache_hit bool. small labels.
sam: worth agreeing on cardinality first — route + model_id is fine, but no user_id or prompt hashes.
dani: ops viewpoint: we need histograms for queue_time + runtime_time at 10ms buckets, and a counter for fallback_reason. low cardinality labels only.
jenna: also add a counter for routing_policy used (e.g., price_pref, latency_pref, region_fallback) — product wants slices.
op s-bot: exporter-created job runtime-metrics-exporter v1 deployed to canary zone at 2024-11-01T16:30Z :white_check_mark:
alex: @maya can you add the new labels to the exporter and open a PR with a tiny compatibility test? please include metrics name prefixes `redwood_runtime_` to avoid collisions.
maya: yup. plan: add gauges/counters: `redwood_runtime_latency_ms_bucket`, `redwood_runtime_queue_ms_bucket`, `redwood_runtime_tokens_total`, `redwood_runtime_fallbacks_total`, labels: ["model", "route", "policy"]
leo: aggregation job questions — retention tiers? raw high-cardinality should be short-lived. propose raw metrics 30d, rollups (hourly) 180d, daily aggregates 365d.
jenna: sounds reasonable. need a cost estimate for 30d raw ingests and monthly rollups before final ok.
sam: aggregation windows: for dashboards we typically need p50/p95/p99 and avg tokens per request. do hourly rollups for up-to-7d, daily after that.
dani: backfill: product requested historical charts for last 90d. if raw only 30d we need to backfill from logs — do we have logs with same fields?
alex: runtime logs currently include model, route, tokens, latency in json. we can backfill but costy. estimate?
maya: rough numbers: ~120M requests/month, avg 3 metrics points each, so ~360M points. Ingest cost approx $0.02/1000 -> ~$7k to backfill 90d? (very rough)
jenna: ok add that to the ticket. product needs cost/benefit.
leo: implementation sketch for aggregation job (sql-ish):
```sql
INSERT INTO metrics_hourly
SELECT
  date_trunc('hour', ts) as hour, model, route,
  approx_quantile(latency_ms, 0.5) as p50,
  approx_quantile(latency_ms, 0.95) as p95,
  approx_quantile(latency_ms, 0.99) as p99,
  sum(tokens) as total_tokens, count(*) as requests
FROM runtime_raw_metrics
WHERE ts >= :start AND ts < :end
GROUP BY hour, model, route;
```
leo: job cadence: hourly for last 7d, daily aggregate job for >7d, monthly rollups for >90d.
sam: one more thing — dashboards need stable route naming. we need a canonicalization step in exporter to strip query params and transform dynamic ids to {id} placeholders.
maya: agreed. i’ll add a small transform map in exporter config: `route_normalizers` with regex rules.
dani: retention policy to lock down: raw 30d, hourly rollups 180d, daily rollups 365d, monthly rollups 3y. backfill: run once for last 90d on request (costed).
jenna: QA items: dashboards should have feature flags behind `dash_runtime_rollout` so we can enable for customers incrementally.
alex: action items: @maya open exporter PR + canary deploy, @leo write aggregation jobs and ticketize backfill cost, @dani confirm retention TTLs with infra billing. @jenna create dashboard templates and QA checklist. set sync next Wed.
maya: on it — PR by EOD tomorrow, will include unit test and normalizers config. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: scheduled job created: metrics-hourly-aggregator cron `0 * * * *` in prod cluster.
jenna: question — alerts? we should add anomaly alert on p99 latency increase >25% over baseline and token-cost per-minute spike.
sam: yep, add alert to the dashboard repo with runbook linking to routing policy rollback procedure.
alex: ok team, thanks. will capture decisions in the RFC draft. :eyes:
